bihar_raw_news.title: Rooftop Solar Subsidies Get a Fresh Push Across Tamil Nadu, Delhi and Bihar
bihar_raw_news.content: Blog Rooftop Solar Subsidies Get a Fresh Push Across Tamil Nadu, Delhi and Bihar Delhi, Bihar, and Tamil Nadu have adopted distinct approaches but share the common goal of providing additional incentives that aim to reduce the upfront cost of rooftop solar and accelerate distributed solar adoption among households. Chitrika Grover 24 Sep 2026 08:49 IST Follow Us Delhi, Bihar and Tamil Nadu have introduced or approved additional financial incentives for residential rooftop solar installations under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, adding state-level support to the central subsidy available to consumers. Advertisment Delhi, Bihar and Tamil Nadu have adopted distinct approaches to supplementing the central subsidy under PM Surya Ghar. While the three states are taking different approaches, the additional incentives aim to reduce the upfront cost of rooftop solar and accelerate distributed solar adoption among households. Advertisment Delhi is providing the largest direct top-up, offering an additional ₹78,000 to eligible households with average monthly electricity consumption below 400 units, while also extending support to Group Housing Societies. Bihar is providing additional state incentives of up to ₹20,000 for a 3 kW system, taking the combined support under the central and state schemes to as much as ₹98,000, while linking rooftop solar with its wider decentralised renewable-energy and solarisation plans. Advertisment Tamil Nadu, meanwhile, has earmarked ₹50 crore to support rooftop solar installations for 1 lakh domestic consumers, with state subsidies ranging from ₹5,000 for systems up to 1 kW to ₹22,000 for systems of 3 kW and above. Delhi Offers Additional Subsidy for Households Using Less Than 400 Units Advertisment The Delhi government has extended an additional rooftop solar subsidy of ₹78,000 under its Top-up Solar (ToP) Scheme, in addition to the subsidy already available under the PM Surya Ghar scheme. The second round of the subsidy targets consumers with an average monthly electricity consumption of less than 400 units. Eligible consumers can have a rooftop solar plant installed without paying the installation cost, subject to the scheme's conditions. Advertisment The Delhi government has also extended the benefits of the ToP Scheme to Group Housing Societies (GHSs). As part of the implementation, the government plans to empanel solar vendors for installing rooftop solar systems of up to 3 kW under the Utility-Led Aggregation (ULA)/Discom Trusteeship Model. Selected vendors will visit eligible consumers' premises after receiving their consent. Bihar Adds State Incentive to PM Surya Ghar Subsidy Bihar has also introduced additional incentives for residential rooftop solar installations through its Mukhyamantri Solar Protsahan Yojana. The state government's additional support is designed to supplement the central financial assistance available under PM Surya Ghar. The combined support can take the subsidy available for a 3 kW rooftop solar system to up to ₹98,000, according to the state government's announcement. Under the structure outlined for the scheme, the central subsidy provides ₹30,000 for a 1 kW system, ₹60,000 for a 2 kW system and ₹78,000 for systems of 3 kW and above. Daily Excelsior 04:29 AM Sep 24, 2026 IST PATNA, Sep 23 : The Bihar Cabinet on Wednesday approved the establishment of Mata Sita University in Patna and Rashtra Kavi Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University in Begusarai. The decisions were taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. Additional Cabinet Secretary Arvind Kumar Choudhary told news persons after the meeting that the Cabinet approved Rs 15 crore each for the establishment of the two universities to meet expenditure on salaries and other establishment-related requirements. Advertisement The proposed university in Patna was initially referred to as Maa Sita University, but the Cabinet approved an amendment changing the name to Mata Sita University. The cabinet also cleared a slew of proposals involving police modernisation, dairy and fisheries development, power sector liabilities and prison reforms. Among the major decisions, the Cabinet sanctioned Rs 24.50 crore for procurement of 50 drones under the centrally sponsored scheme for assistance to states and union Territories for police modernisation. The drones are intended for crowd-control and management, riverine and anti-Naxal operations, disaster management and other policing requirements, 8nforned Choudhary. An additional Rs 33.685 crore was approved for procurement of equipment and other items for district police, railway police, the Bihar Special Armed Police, the Prohibition Department and the State Narcotics Control Bureau, among other agencies. The Cabinet also approved a one-time remission measure for eligible convicted prisoners to facilitate their release from jails on the occasion of Mahatma Gandhi''s birth anniversary on October 2, 2026. It further approved amendments to Rule 743 of the Bihar Prison Manual, 2012, in accordance with the Supreme Court''s orders of July 30 and September 10, 2026, in the case concerning discrimination inside prisons. For the agriculture and livestock sector, the Cabinet approved the state scheme Mukhyamantri Gaudhan Vikas Rin Yojana for 2026-27 to 2028-29, involving an estimated expenditure of Rs 160.001 crore. The government also approved release of Rs 757.63 crore to Bihar State Power (Holding) Company Ltd in five equal instalments towards unfunded terminal benefit liabilities of former Bihar State Electricity Board employees up to October 31, 2012. Under Saat Nischay-3, the Cabinet approved a Rs 126.07-crore dairy development programme in Supaul, Madhepura and Saharsa districts. The programme includes setting up a curd plant, premium ice-cream plant, Total Mixed Ration plant, buffalo heifer farm, use of sex-sorted semen, formation of new dairy cooperative societies and installation of milk chilling infrastructure. A Rs 195.28-crore project under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) was also approved for transforming the Siwan wetlands cluster in Basantpur, Bhagwanpur Hat and Goriakothi into an integrated aquaculture and export-oriented value chain.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will interact today via video conference with participants of Seva Yatra travelling from Vadnagar to Varanasi under Seva Sankalp Abhiyan. The interaction with the Prime Minister will give the Seva Yatris a chance to share their experiences from the journey, which is intended to connect youth participation and community service across the locations covered by the teams. The Seva Yatra began on September 17 and is part of the wider ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ to highlight PM Modi’s 25 years of public life. The participants are travelling through towns, districts, talukas and villages, with the programme focusing on taking community service and public engagement activities to the grassroots. The journey is not limited to a motorcycle expedition, but is designed to bring together service, communication, youth participation, social welfare, cultural connect and community mobilisation at different locations along the route. Ten groups are undertaking the Vadnagar-to-Varanasi journey. The two-way motorcycle yatras between Vadnagar and Varanasi involve young participants travelling across multiple states, districts and villages. During the journey, the Seva Yatris have engaged with local communities and participated in service-oriented activities. These include cleanliness drives and interactions with beneficiaries and residents, as well as activities at schools, hospitals, nursing homes, and other community locations. The journey is scheduled to continue until October 7. The broader campaign was launched from Vadnagar on September 17 by Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, with the Vadnagar-to-Varanasi bike yatra being flagged off as part of the initiative. The wider motorcycle initiative includes journeys in both directions between Vadnagar, associated with PM Modi’s early life, and Varanasi, his Lok Sabha constituency.

national_raw_news.title: 46 mins ago | Regional News 39 Uttar Pradesh CM launches Bharat Taxi, Krishak Samriddhi Yojana
national_raw_news.content: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath launched Bharat Taxi and Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana, taking two major steps for taxi drivers and farmers. Through ‘Bharat Taxi’, two-wheeler, taxi and three-wheeler drivers will be able to join on zero commission upon registration. They will also receive social security of 5 lakh rupees. Its operations have started in Lucknow, Gorakhpur, Varanasi and Prayagraj. MOUs have also been signed with various institutions, including Lucknow Airport, Lucknow Metro and Lucknow Police. Referring to Prayagraj Mahakumbh 2025, CM noted that Lakhs of young people helped devotees to reach Sangam on their bikes through Rapido. They also helped pilgrims to reach railway station and airport from Sangam. Under Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana, the interest rate on loans provided to farmers through the Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Gramya Vikas Bank has been reduced from 11% to 6%. Chief Minister said, to ensure that farmers do not face a shortage of funds for farming and machinery, arrangements have been made for long-term loans. In the coming years, the target is to provide its benefits to five lakh small and marginal farmers. CM Yogi said since the formation of his government in 2017, loans worth more than 36,000 crore rupees of 86 lakh small and marginal farmers were waived off. Irrigation projects that had remained pending for decades were completed. CM Yogi stated that 122 sugar mills are currently operational in the state. More than 100 of these mills are making sugarcane payments on the fourth day. Over the past nine years, sugarcane payments amounting to 3.30 lakh crore rupees have been made to farmers. He alleged that previous governments had shut down 29 sugar mills, of which 21 were sold at throwaway prices.
